cases.title: Six airports: concentration by policy design
cases.question: Did uncapped awards trade away resilience and comparable operator performance, and what would distinguish that choice from bidder-specific favour?
cases.finding: DEA recommended a two-airport cap; the final appraisal retained EGoS’s no-cap design and AEL later topped all six bids. The records establish a concentration-risk decision. They do not establish secret coordination. Competitive bid counts and the dismissed Thiruvananthapuram challenge narrow the theory.

claims.text: The attached DEA appraisal recommends no more than two airports per bidder; the final minutes retain an uncapped design.
claims.response: The committee adopted other safeguards and accepted a different institutional risk trade-off.
claims.alternative: Broadening entry and transaction scale may have been intended to improve competition and execution.
claims.falsifier: A binding final cap or a corrected signed minute would overturn this reading.
missingRecords: Final RFP, signed concessions and complete EGoS minutes

claims.text: AEL’s six highest bids establish the outcome, not a privately agreed winner.
claims.response: The Ministry says 32 bids came from 10 entities and the successful bidder was not known during design.
claims.alternative: A capital-rich entrant may lawfully outbid rivals under common published terms.
claims.falsifier: Contemporaneous nonpublic specifications or communications tied to one bidder, corroborated independently, would require reassessment.
missingRecords: All bidder technical/financial scores, common clarifications and contemporaneous representations

claims.text: The 2022 Supreme Court order dismissed the connected Thiruvananthapuram petitions.
claims.response: The order cites the agreed preference range, ₹168/₹135 bid gap, employee options and existing operations.
claims.alternative: The policy can be legally sustainable while still requiring competition and performance assessment.
claims.falsifier: A later review or contrary order addressing the same disposition would change the legal-status entry.
missingRecords: Official signed court copy and any later review disposition

whatWeKnow: The policy choice preceded the financial-bid outcome.
The DEA recommendation is advisory, so awarding more than two airports did not breach that unadopted recommendation.
The minutes changed several safeguards, including performance security, rather than simply accepting every draft term.

In light of uncapped awards, AAI raised the proposed net-worth requirement to ₹1,000 crore; the minutes also revised the single-project technical-capacity threshold upward. These safeguards matter when evaluating the rejected cap.
The Court rejected the specific challenge; no finding of hidden collusion was identified in these inspected records.
whatWeDoNotKnow: Full bidder-level qualification and pricing data for all six airports are not assembled.
Whether later capital spending, service quality or termination risk were better or worse under concentrated ownership is untested.
No source inspected establishes a private inducement, side payment or winner-specific direction.

limits: Selected institutional decision file; not a census of airport privatisation or all Modi government decisions.
Legal authority differs from good policy: a lawful concentration choice can still create resilience questions.
The government’s 2006 traffic comparator concerns different years and portfolios; it is not a controlled estimate.

The minutes record project-cost uncertainty, a rapid timetable and functional brownfield airports; future winner and long-run results were not yet known.

options.label: Cap the number of awards
options.expectedObservableOutcome: More operators available for comparison and fallback; possibly lower best-bid revenue or reduced participation.

options.label: Allow uncapped awards with capacity and performance safeguards
options.expectedObservableOutcome: One entity may win several airports if it leads each price comparison; assess common-mode performance exposure afterwards.

options.label: Phase awards and publish a common performance baseline
options.expectedObservableOutcome: Would permit learning and comparison, with a longer transaction timetable. Analytical oversight option, not recorded as the adopted policy.

decisionAnalysis.observedOutcome: Government reports AEL highest in all six tenders. The later 2022 order dismissed the Thiruvananthapuram challenge. No matched post-concession service or welfare comparison has been completed here.
hindsightLimits: Retrospective reconstruction, not recovered private preferences or a calculated game-theoretic equilibrium.
All tests were formulated after the bid and court outcomes were known; no predictive accuracy is claimed.

hypothesis.proposition: An uncapped simultaneous tender can concentrate operational exposure and reduce later comparison across operators even when each award follows published price rules. Whether bidder-specific influence contributed is an unanswered evidence question.
hypothesis.assessmentReason: A deliberate risk trade-off and concentrated winning-bid outcome are documented. The stronger claim of a secretly predetermined winner is unsupported; the government response and Court disposition are material counterevidence.
hypothesis.jurisdiction: Union MoCA, AAI, airport EGoS and PPPAC set and appraise this tender. Kerala’s state-backed bidder and its limited right of first refusal do not control the Union process.

rules.title: 85th PPPAC airport transaction conditions
rules.operativePeriod: Appraisal 11 December 2018; tender and signed concession must be checked for final operative text
rules.requirement: No award cap and no prior airport experience prerequisite were retained. Revised capacity, termination and performance-security conditions were recommended. DEA’s proposed cap did not become a prohibition.

cases.title: Coal auctions: the discretionary second attempt
cases.question: When a mine repeatedly attracts one bidder, do published reasons and comparable outcomes justify allocation, or does discretion conceal unequal treatment?
cases.finding: A second-attempt lone bid can lawfully reach ECoS for a decision; it is not automatically awarded. The 2025 record includes security-return notices for first-attempt lone bids and substantial competition at other mines. Mine-level reasons for the three observed second-attempt lone bids remain missing.

geography.basis: Institutional authority, not a mine or money-transfer address

geography.label: Jharkhand — round 16 second-attempt offer
geography.basis: October 2026 briefing lists one partially explored second-attempt round 15 mine in Jharkhand; do not infer it is a named 2025 block

claims.text: The Ministry reports eleven ECoS-approved second-attempt single-bid allocations as of 20 October 2023.
claims.response: The stated rationale is reasonable offers, repeated unsuccessful offerings and increased production rather than revenue maximisation.
claims.alternative: Lone bids may reflect difficult geology, clearance risk, infrastructure or weak demand.
claims.falsifier: Mine-level records showing no such approvals, or later correction of the count, would overturn the aggregate.
missingRecords: Mine-level ECoS reasons, offers, valuation benchmarks and actual vesting orders

claims.text: Two first-attempt lone-bid blocks in the 2025 opening received bid-security-return notices, not listed closing awards in the inspected overall result.
claims.response: The published notice identifies Amalgam Steel and Sunflag separately; it does not confirm actual bank-guarantee collection.
claims.alternative: The published minimum-participation filter may be operating normally.
claims.falsifier: A contemporaneous award or corrected notice for those same stages would change the reading.

claims.text: The June 2025 opening and August 2025 overall result cannot be treated as one identical denominator.
claims.response: The opening excludes six underground blocks; the result includes two Rajgamar entries not in that opening table.
claims.alternative: Different subrounds, schedules and geological categories explain the apparent mismatch.
claims.falsifier: A complete matching tranche/block ledger showing identical populations would invalidate this caution.
missingRecords: Full tranche register, block identifiers, amendments and cancelled/rolled-over statuses

whatWeKnow: June 16 opening: 41 bids across 11 blocks; three were second-attempt round 11 lone bids.
Patal East (Western Part) and Tambia South are first-attempt lone-bid examples with August 26 security-return instructions.
Phutamura had 13 opening bids and a 65.25% closing revenue-share bid; Mahuagarhi had 4 and 7%. These are different mines, not matched values.
The October 7, 2026 briefing still bars affiliate bids for the same mine and identifies lower 2% floor for underground mines versus 4% generally.
whatWeDoNotKnow: The inspected records do not resolve ECoS decisions or final vesting for Jawardaha South, Margo East and Margo West.
Opening-count tables cannot assign each company to each block without a linked evaluation record.
No bidder coordination, suppressed rival, political payment or beneficial-ownership link is established.
Complete binding tender versions and exact effective dates for each rule variation have not been acquired.

Low bid participation is an investigative lead with several ordinary explanations, not a collusion verdict.
Revenue-share bids, projected capacity revenues, refundable guarantees and realised state receipts are separate stages.

actors.incentive: Institutional trade-off: accelerate development while requiring a reasonable offer and transparent process. No private preference inferred.

informationThen.text: By October 2023 the Ministry reported many repeatedly unbid mines and 11 single-bid approvals; this is the public rationale available at that date, not the later 2025 outcome.

options.label: Reoffer a lone-bid mine and publish reasons
options.expectedObservableOutcome: Potentially more participation, but delayed development or repeated no-bid rounds.

options.expectedObservableOutcome: Faster allocation is possible; reasoned comparable valuation and development tracking are needed to assess public value.

options.label: Annul an insufficiently competitive first attempt and return bid security
options.expectedObservableOutcome: Records should distinguish return instructions from bank release, and later reoffers from current awards.

decisionAnalysis.observedOutcome: The later December 2024 briefing retains a minimum-two-qualified-bidder rule and affiliate restriction; the binding tender must resolve special second-attempt treatment. The 2025 sample shows both multi-bid closing outcomes and first-attempt security-return notices. Three observed second-attempt lone bids cannot be followed to a decision in the records acquired. The 2026 round 16 schedule remains future.
hindsightLimits: The 2023 date anchors the published rationale, not the original 2020 adoption or every later decision.
Tests were formulated after 2025 outcomes were inspected; no ex-ante win, causal effect or guilt probability is claimed.

hypothesis.proposition: Discretion over repeatedly unbid mines may weaken comparable price discovery if mine-specific reasons and alternatives are not published. Unequal treatment is testable only after matching comparable blocks, bidders and decision stages.
hypothesis.assessmentReason: Discretion is publicly acknowledged and does not automatically establish irregularity. First-attempt security-return instructions and competitive closing bids contradict a universal automatic-allocation story. The three second-attempt dispositions remain unresolved.
hypothesis.jurisdiction: Union Ministry of Coal / Nominated Authority and ECoS manage auction decisions. State mineral leases, land/forest permissions, royalties and local impacts require separate records; auction approval does not replace those powers.

rules.title: Commercial single-bid methodology as explained by the Ministry
rules.operativePeriod: Publicly described 20 October 2023; confirm binding tender for each decision
rules.requirement: First attempt below two technically qualified bidders is annulled; a lone bidder again in the second attempt is referred to ECoS for appropriate decision.

rules.title: December 2024 commercial auction briefing
rules.operativePeriod: Applies to the identified 2024/2025 tranches, subject to binding tender
rules.requirement: The briefing sets a 4% revenue-share floor, rejects affiliates bidding for the same mine, and describes minimum qualified participation. The agreement/tender prevails.

rules.title: October 2026 round 16 briefing
rules.operativePeriod: Published 7 October 2026 for the scheduled round 16 and round 15 second attempt
rules.requirement: General 4% and underground 2% floors, affiliate restriction and minimum-participation language are in the briefing. The exact date and instrument introducing changes is not established here.

alternatives.label: Unproved selective discretion
alternatives.explanation: Similar mines or bidders may receive inconsistent treatment without a documented public-interest rationale.
alternatives.discriminatingRecord: Mine-matched ECoS reasons, offer benchmarks, conflict/affiliate declarations and contemporaneous objections

alternatives.label: Lawful production and scarcity trade-off
alternatives.explanation: Unattractive or partially explored blocks may repeatedly draw one/no bidder; a reasoned allocation can advance production despite lower bid pressure.
alternatives.discriminatingRecord: Geology/clearance/infrastructure-adjusted comparator set, development milestones and actual production/receipts

alternatives.label: Mixed populations and financial stages
alternatives.explanation: Tranches, first versus second attempts, underground exclusions and proposed versus paid figures can manufacture a pattern.
alternatives.discriminatingRecord: Stable block IDs with full bid-opening, qualification, results, vesting and payment dates

tests.question: Does every lone bid become an allocation?
tests.expectedIfTrue: An automatic-allocation story would predict award progression for every lone-bid block.
tests.expectedIfAlternative: First-attempt annulment/security return and documented separate second-attempt referrals.
tests.observation: The August 26 notice instructs security return for Patal East and Tambia South, directly narrowing the automatic-allocation idea.

tests.question: Are second-attempt decisions consistent across comparable mines?
tests.expectedIfTrue: Unexplained selective approvals or systematically weak offers after adjustment would support a concern.
tests.expectedIfAlternative: Documented offer reasonableness, comparable rejection/approval criteria and subsequent production would support the declared policy.
tests.observation: Three June 2025 second-attempt lone-bid blocks identified; no mine-level ECoS decision obtained.
tests.nextRecord: Reasoned ECoS decisions for Jawardaha South, Margo East, Margo West and a matched mine set

tests.question: Will the published round 16 schedule produce traceable bid and decision records?
tests.expectedIfTrue: Opaque or inconsistent publication would preserve an oversight gap, not prove wrongdoing.
tests.expectedIfAlternative: Dated opening/evaluation/result records permit exact-mine reconciliation including any second attempt.
tests.observation: October 7 briefing schedules bids November 9 and e-auctions December 3–10, 2026; these events are future as of review.
tests.nextRecord: Future round 16 notices, any schedule amendments and exact block/tranche status register

proposedLinks.question: Was the observed second-attempt lone bid referred, approved, rejected or left pending?
proposedLinks.missingEvidence: Mine-specific referral, reasoned committee decision and any vesting order.
proposedLinks.disconfirmingEvidence: A documented withdrawal, rejection or different mine identity would disconfirm an approval link.

proposedLinks.question: What decision followed this second-attempt lone bid?
proposedLinks.missingEvidence: Exact mine/tranche committee file and outcome record.
proposedLinks.disconfirmingEvidence: A record establishing no referral or a rejected/withdrawn bid; do not infer allocation from the opening table.

proposedLinks.question: Is there a documented second-attempt allocation decision for this block?
proposedLinks.missingEvidence: Exact decision and terms, linked by stable mine ID to the June 2025 bid.
proposedLinks.disconfirmingEvidence: Contrary official disposition or a nonmatching mine/tranche shows the proposed join fails.

chronology.event: Ministry describes eleven approved repeated-single-bid allocations and its production objective.
Briefing describes auction floor, affiliate and qualification rules for the forthcoming tranches.
Bid-opening release separately lists round 12 and round 11 second-attempt blocks.
Seven closing bids published for the overall round 12 result.
Security-return notice identifies two first-attempt single-bid mines and their bidders.
Round 16 briefing publishes changed population/counts and future November/December schedule.

hypothesis.comparison: Use all offered blocks, including no bids, returned securities and unsuccessful reoffers. Match geology, exploration, mine type, clearances, transport, reserve quality and date before comparing prices; first and second attempts are distinct strata.
inferenceLimits: Retrospective reconstruction, not a preregistered prediction.
Future schedule is observed publication; future auction outcomes are not known.
No inferred bid rigging, private payment, total public loss or model probability.
A security-return instruction is not an actual refund; a closing bid is not vested ownership or cash receipt.

rejectedJoins.proposed: Uncapped terms prove a secretly selected beneficiary
rejectedJoins.reason: Temporal sequence and a policy benefit do not establish communications, inducement or intent. Keep the question separate from observed edges.

rejectedJoins.proposed: Awarding six airports violated a binding two-airport rule
rejectedJoins.reason: The two-airport cap was an appraisal recommendation; the recorded final choice retained no cap.

rejectedJoins.proposed: One bid in the opening table proves ECoS allocation
rejectedJoins.reason: Bid receipt precedes qualification, referral, decision and vesting. No mine-specific approval inspected.

rejectedJoins.proposed: Return notice proves cash transferred or guarantee actually released
rejectedJoins.reason: The notice is a collection instruction, not a bank confirmation; no amount is published.

rejectedJoins.reason: The index says 14 rounds while the later briefing says 15; reporting vintages and definitions differ.
